title: Oil Buyers Battered by the Iran War Energy Crisis Race to Build Buffers
partialText: As rising fuel costs clobber their economies, the Philippines and other developing countries in Asia are pushing to build strategic petroleum reserves to cushion against future shocks.

title: Lebanese Army Accuses Israeli Troops of Firing as Its Forces Deploy in ‘Pilot Zone’
partialText: The Israeli military was withdrawing from a village under a U.S.-brokered deal to transfer control of occupied areas to Lebanon after months of war. The Israeli military did not immediately comment.

title: Pentagon Identifies Soldier Killed in Iran War as Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton
partialText: Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton, the 17th service member to be named, was killed during the disposal of a drone in northern Iraq.

title: Trump Escalates Canada Tariffs as Mark Carney Holds Firm
partialText: The president’s new tariffs on a top U.S. trading partner aim at gaining concessions, but the Canadian government, and the public, have been bracing for the escalation.

title: 1,700 H.I.V. Treatment Sites Closed After Trump Aid Cuts, a Study Finds
partialText: New research also shows that children and high-risk adult populations have been particularly affected.

title: Cameron Hamilton Poised to Lead FEMA Once More
partialText: Cameron Hamilton defended the agency last year when President Trump talked about eliminating it. Emergency managers hope for more stability if he’s confirmed as administrator.

title: Google Releases Three New Gemini A.I. Models
partialText: The models include one that is the company’s most powerful and another that is fine-tuned for cybersecurity, as Google competes with rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: How Republicans Made Olive Garden Into a Voter ID Talking Point
partialText: Republicans claim that Olive Garden polices its Never-Ending Pasta Bowl more tightly than the United States does its elections. It’s not that simple.

title: Democrats’ Top Senate Candidate in Maine Won’t Support Schumer for Leader
partialText: Troy Jackson, who is set to become the party’s nominee, also said in an interview that he was not sure he wanted the support of Senator Chuck Schumer in the general election.

title: What We Know About Tuesday’s Arizona Primaries
partialText: Arizona primary voters will choose nominees for governor, secretary of state and for key races that could determine control of the House.

title: Why Does This Jacket Cost $770? Because It Made Me a New Man.
partialText: Lots of men are geeking out over very expensive clothes — and I became one of them.

title: France Is Poised to Restrict Social Media for Children
partialText: Its new law, which would be the first of its kind enacted by a European country, would ban access to some accounts for anyone under 15.

title: A Family’s Daring Escape From North Korea
partialText: Their resolve for freedom hardened during the pandemic, when they lived through a crippling food shortage and were forced to witness frequent public executions.

title: How a 911 Call Led to the Nation’s Strictest Trans Bathroom Law
partialText: People in Sandpoint, Idaho, don’t know how to characterize a woman’s brush with a transgender woman in a Y.M.C.A. locker room, but the emergency call that followed is still reverberating.

title: Cyclospora Spreads Through Human Feces. How Did It Get Into Our Food Supply?
partialText: The large number of cases suggests that excrement entered the food system on a “surprising scale.”

title: Why States Are Making It Harder to Save Money With Solar Panels
partialText: The changes are costing homeowners money. But they also reflect a changing grid — and the need for home batteries.

title: The U.S. Is Pulling Back on Energy Efficiency
partialText: The Trump administration is undoing fuel-saving efforts even as war in Iran, data centers and heat waves are pushing up gasoline and electricity costs.

title: In Venezuela’s Rubble, a Search for the Family Pets
partialText: Volunteers are reuniting pets with families, offering Venezuelans comfort amid loss and devastation.

title: ‘Too Rare to Care’? A New Center for Rare Diseases Hopes to Change That
partialText: A new nonprofit wants to streamline gene therapy for diseases often avoided by pharmaceutical companies — making treatment more like a routine procedure than a bespoke drug.

title: The Best Genetic Risk Tools Don’t Work Equally for Everyone
partialText: Genetic prediction models are poised to revolutionize medicine. But because they have been trained on European DNA, they threaten to widen health care disparities.

title: Restaurant Review: Chez Panisse and Bar Panisse in Berkeley
partialText: The Bay Area farm-to-table classic changed the American restaurant scene. Now it has opened a dynamic new place right next door.

partialText: Israel has not been held accountable for its actions in Gaza. The nation and the individuals and countries enabling it to escape punishment may only benefit.

title: Lives Lost
partialText: We look at the American casualties in the war with Iran.

title: The Ordeal of a 42-Day Hantavirus Quarantine: ‘I Felt Like a Prisoner’
partialText: Eighteen Americans were isolated for weeks in a Nebraska quarantine facility after being exposed to the deadly virus on a cruise ship. Many found the experience traumatic.
